title: How to choose a workflow automation platform
summary: Compare automation workflows by execution pattern, billing unit, hosting needs and what their exports can recover.

sections.heading: Map the real workload
paragraphs: Write down the trigger frequency, records or bundles processed, action modules, retries and peak bursts for one representative workflow. Make documents both fixed and dynamic credit consumption; AI and advanced modules can vary with tokens, file size, pages or runtime. Compare observed usage to each vendor's current unit rather than treating a scenario, operation, credit and execution as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Choose who operates the workflow
paragraphs: Make presents a hosted visual scenario workflow. n8n documents both Cloud and self-hosted options. For self-hosting, include the operator's work for deployment, credentials, updates, backups, monitoring, TLS and encryption at rest. n8n also documents usage-data processing from self-hosted deployments unless users opt out. Review the current license and plan entitlements for the exact use case before choosing a deployment path.

sections.heading: Trial failure and recovery
paragraphs: Run a bounded test with representative but non-sensitive data. Force a timeout or malformed response, inspect retry and duplicate behavior, and verify how credentials are stored. For Make, its docs describe importing an individual JSON blueprint, recreating account connections and a 2 MB file ceiling; n8n documents separate workflow, package and instance-backup paths. Rehearse the needed recovery scope in a separate environment, and inspect exports for secrets before depending on them in production.

pros.text: Make documents fixed and dynamic credits, giving teams billing rules they can apply to a measured workflow.
Make documents JSON blueprints for reusing or backing up individual scenarios, with account connections recreated after import.
n8n documents both Cloud and self-hosted deployment paths, so teams can evaluate different operating models.

cons.text: Make's dynamic modules can consume credits based on tokens, file size, pages or processing time, which makes workload measurement important.
The self-host option in n8n documentation does not establish lower total cost; deployment and ongoing operation still need a use-case-specific estimate, including TLS and at-rest encryption.
Make warns that a simple-mode AES key is exposed when sharing a scenario or downloading its blueprint; inspect an export for secrets before distribution.

faqs.question: How can I compare automation costs fairly?
faqs.answer: Estimate a representative workflow's frequency, processed bundles, actions and retries, then apply each platform's current billing rules. Make documents fixed and dynamic credits; this is a reason to measure your own workload rather than assume a universal conversion.

faqs.question: Is self-hosting automatically less expensive?
faqs.answer: The docs establish a self-hosting option, not a lower total cost. Include infrastructure and the operator's work, and confirm the applicable n8n license and plan terms.

faqs.question: Does self-hosting eliminate n8n usage data processing?
faqs.answer: No. n8n's privacy policy says certain usage data is processed unless users opt out. Verify the selected instance's setting and connected-service terms.

faqs.question: What if the automation platform will host workflows for my customers?
faqs.answer: n8n's support guidance says hosting and managing clients' workflows and credentials in your own instance requires Enterprise, while embedding n8n to expose workflows to customers requires a white-labeled Embed license. Consulting on a client's own internal instance does not itself require a commercial license for the consultant. Confirm the exact service and license with n8n; this is vendor guidance, not a legal determination.

faqs.question: What should I include in an n8n migration plan?
faqs.answer: n8n supports workflow JSON export/import and an n8n CLI package path that is still in Preview. CLI backups cover workflows and credentials, not users/roles, execution history/logs, variables or instance settings such as the encryption key. Full recovery may also require the `.n8n` folder, database, external storage and custom nodes. Protect exports because workflow JSON may expose credential names or authentication headers; test the exact move before relying on it.

faqs.question: How should I interpret Make's published privacy and retention statements?
faqs.answer: Make's privacy notice describes application-related usage data; its Privacy & GDPR page says personal data can be requested for deletion once no longer needed, and its security page states that log data is kept for 30 days by default with an Enterprise extension option. These vendor-wide statements do not identify a workspace's settings, all workflow-data categories or purge timing.

faqs.question: What can I recover from a Make scenario blueprint?
faqs.answer: Make documents a JSON blueprint containing scenario modules, module settings and mapped values, and says it can be used to back up a scenario when switching Make accounts. After import, create the account connections again; the file must be under 2 MB. Scenario history has a separate CSV export. This does not establish full-organization recovery, and no import or migration was tested.

faqs.question: Can an exported Make blueprint contain a secret?
faqs.answer: Make warns that a simple-mode AES secret key is exposed when a scenario is shared or its blueprint is downloaded. Inspect the workflow for hard-coded secrets before export or sharing, and use approved secret handling.

faqs.question: Can n8n use a locally run model in an automation?
faqs.answer: n8n documents an Ollama Chat Model and a self-hosted AI Starter Kit pairing n8n with Ollama for local LLMs. The Ollama credential defaults to a local URL and also supports remote authenticated endpoints; containers may need network configuration. n8n describes the kit as a proof-of-concept/demo and says to harden it before production. Confirm the target endpoint, workflow data path and model behavior; no inference was tested.

faqs.question: What should a trial prove before automation goes live?
faqs.answer: Test a normal run, a failed run and recovery with representative data; confirm credential handling and export or rollback before connecting a production workflow.

verdict: Choose based on a measured workflow and the operating model you can support; neither a credit count nor a self-host option proves the total cost or production fit on its own.
bestFor: Teams comparing hosted visual automation with configurable Cloud or self-hosted workflows
notFor: Readers looking for a universal cost winner or an unverified production recommendation
migration: Export a representative Make scenario as a JSON blueprint, recreate its account connections after import, and check the documented 2 MB limit; export history separately as CSV if needed. Compare that scenario-level path with the precise n8n workflow/package/instance recovery scope required. Inspect exports for simple-mode AES keys, then rehearse the move in a separate environment; no cross-platform migration was tested.
gaps: For 10,000 monthly credits, Make lists USD 12/month with monthly payment or USD 9/month equivalent on annual billing. Confirm checkout taxes and whether a selectable region meets the intended residency requirement; verify workspace-specific data scope, configured log retention, connected-provider terms, deletion timing, applicable DPA and representative workflow behavior. No account, legal or hands-on workflow review was performed.
Verify n8n self-hosted telemetry opt-out and connected-service data terms; no instance configuration was inspected.
Check the exact client-facing or embedded service against n8n's current license and plan; published use-case examples do not determine an individual deployment's entitlements.
Verify the Make organization resources and n8n instance scope that must move; their documented scenario/workflow/package/backup paths cover distinct objects, and no move or full restore was tested.
Verify that the target n8n deployment can reach its Ollama endpoint and that the model, network and workflow data path satisfy the intended use; no inference or self-hosted setup was tested.
